task_instance: Create a minimal Cloudflare Worker project (wrangler.jsonc config + src/index.js handler) and use a Wrangler CLI already cached on disk (from a prior npx run, under /root/.npm/_npx/.../node_modules/wrangler, including the bundled workerd binary) to validate the config/build with `wrangler deploy --dry-run` and to actually run the Worker locally with `wrangler dev --local`, verifying it serves a real HTTP response, with no network access.
tools_used: wrangler CLI (pre-cached copy, no install performed)
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/cloudflare__skills__wrangler@offline-workstation . Created wrangler.jsonc ({name: offline-demo-worker, main: src/index.js, compatibility_date: 2026-09-27}) and src/index.js (a fetch handler returning 'Hello from offline Worker!'). Did NOT install anything: found an existing cached Wrangler package (v4.141.0) plus its bundled workerd binary already present on disk at /root/.npm/_npx/32026684e21afda6/node_modules/wrangler (left over from a prior process) and invoked it directly via `node .../wrangler/bin/wrangler.js`. Unset HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY to rule out use of the sandbox's outbound proxy, i.e. ran fully network-isolated. `node wrangler.js deploy --dry-run` (from work dir) exited 0 and printed 'Total Upload: 0.26 KiB / gzip: 0.20 KiB / No bindings found. / --dry-run: exiting now.' -- confirming the config parses and the Worker bundles/packages correctly. Then ran `node wrangler.js dev --local --port 18787 --ip 127.0.0.1` in the background; it printed a harmless network-dependent warning ('Unable to fetch the `Request.cf` object! ... Host not i... is not valid JSON' -- an expected offline artifact) but still started a local server ('Ready on http://127.0.0.1:18787'). `curl -m 5 http://127.0.0.1:18787/` returned the exact body 'Hello from offline Worker!', proving the Worker actually ran and served a request purely locally. Background wrangler/workerd processes (PIDs 8029, 8037, 8057, 8139) were then killed to clean up. This exercises the skill's core deliverable -- configuring a Worker project and validating it via Wrangler's local dev and dry-run deploy commands -- entirely offline. Note: this required a pre-existing cached Wrangler install; on a truly bare offline workstation with no such cache and no lockfile-based node_modules already present, installing Wrangler would require network access (npm registry) and would be a missing_tool_in_runtime blocker instead.
